text: Git branching is an important part of modern version control. A branch lets you work on new code without changing the main project. Developers often create feature branches to build a new function or fix a bug safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main line. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request, so others can review the changes and discuss them. This workflow keeps the project stable and organized. It also helps teams work together, because everyone can develop in parallel and combine their work step by step.
